rules.rule: As an unmarried partner on a first New Year visit you are not expected to give the elders red envelopes (the custom runs elder → younger, married → unmarried); bring gifts for the parents instead. If the family has young children (the partner's younger siblings, nieces, nephews), many visitors give each child an envelope — the same amount for each, a round even sum (one zhihu article: 50–200 yuan is common for minors); some also give close grandparents 100–500 yuan with a written wish. Be ready to receive one yourself: parents often give a partner they meet for the first time a red envelope (见面礼). Ask your partner what the family and province expect before you go.
rules.why: Customs differ by province and family, and both giving too little and giving where it is not expected can embarrass people.
rules.regional_note: Amounts differ widely: Guangdong is modest (利是 of 5–50 yuan), Zhejiang, Fujian, Jiangsu and Shanghai are among the most generous (see rule amounts).

rules.rule: Avoid amounts containing 4 (四 sì sounds like 死 sǐ, death) and 250 (二百五 means “idiot”); prefer even sums and 6s and 8s (e.g. 200, 600, 666, 800, 888); give children of the same family the same amount. Typical sums vary enormously: Guangdong 利是 are often 5–10 yuan (50 already counts as generous), while 2026 media figures put ordinary relatives' children at about 200–500 yuan and close relatives at 666–2,000 in Zhejiang or Shanghai, and 500–1,000 for ordinary relatives in parts of Fujian; the north starts around 100. The often-shared “national red-envelope map” is 2018 data.
rules.why: Numbers carry meaning (homophones), and the expected amount depends on region, closeness and income.
rules.regional_note: Guangdong: small and widespread; Zhejiang/Fujian/Jiangsu/Shanghai: large; ask the partner for the family's usual figure.

rules.rule: A token refusal is optional: it is more common with relatives you are not close to, while from close elders you accept graciously; there is no fixed number of refusals. Red envelopes are reciprocal (礼尚往来): if relatives give your children — or you — red envelopes, your side is expected to return the gesture to their children at a suitable moment.
rules.why: Families keep the exchange balanced (礼尚往来).

sources.title: 当亲戚赠与我们红包时，我们为什么要在表面上过分推辞？我们该不该这么做？ - 知乎
sources.publisher: 知乎 Zhihu (community Q&A)
sources.evidence: Search summary of this and related posts (zhihu.com/question/513979659 “怎样教孩子收红包礼仪？”, zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/602649524, zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/20161267814): refusing has no fixed pattern and can be skipped — “若收红包，请双手接，给长辈敬个礼。并说‘谢谢’”; if you will accept anyway, ritual refusal is unnecessary, accept calmly and say thanks; refusing is more common with relatives you are not close to, as a show of politeness; a suggested blessing when receiving: bow and say “祝您新年快乐，恭喜发财，身体健康”; take the envelope with both hands; never open it in front of the giver (look at home); do not announce the amount. No source gave a fixed number of refusals.

sources.evidence: Search summary of this and related questions (zhihu.com/question/442420115 “第一次跟男朋友（广东人）去他家见爸妈，但是没收到红包是什么意思？”, zhihu.com/question/67478834 “带女朋友第一次正式见我父母，应该给多少红包？”, zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/19321479715): no fixed rule, it depends on local custom; “长辈给晚辈、已婚给未婚发红包，所以未婚男友不一定需要给长辈发红包”, “一般是过年时长辈包给小孩，已婚给未婚，领导给下属”; some places expect a return gift on the first visit and gifts for the family are appropriate; for close grandparents “他们并不在乎红包金额的大小”, 100–500 yuan with a written blessing is a common range, or gifts (烟酒、水果) plus a red envelope; if the girlfriend has under-age younger siblings, give each one an envelope, “数目是百的偶数就可以了”; another article: 50–200 yuan is a common range for minors; give several children the same amount; avoid 4 and 250; safest is to ask the partner about the family’s custom.

rules.rule: WeChat red packets are now a standard part of New Year greetings in family and work groups. A luck-based group packet (拼手气红包) splits the sum at random (decided by WeChat's server; 手气最佳 is pure luck), an ordinary one (普通红包) splits it equally; a red packet — and each share of a group packet — is capped at 200 yuan. If the only card in your WeChat Pay is a foreign one, you cannot send or receive red packets or transfers: they need a mainland Chinese bank card (Shanghai government payment guide; 2026 guides incl. LTL), though merchant QR payments work. Ask your partner to send one for you, or give a paper envelope.
rules.why: Digital red packets are a common way to send New Year greetings to friends, coworkers and relatives far away (LTL; CCTV: 手机里的电子红包).

sources.title: 抢微信红包有没有“最佳手气”攻略？红包上限为什么是200元？微信回应

sources.evidence: Search summary (also thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32625313 “第二个抢微信红包最容易手气最佳？微信官方回应”): WeChat says the amount of each share is randomly assigned by the server when the packet is created, so “手气最佳” (best luck) tips have no basis; people prefer the luck-based (手气) red packet to the ordinary one with equal shares; the headline refers to a 200-yuan upper limit per red packet. “Whoever gets 手气最佳 sends the next one” is a group game, not a universal rule (summary of zhihu “微信群红包的47种玩法”); a school study is summarised as “抢红包人数会影响‘手气王’概率吗？”. No source for a “谢谢老板” etiquette rule was found.

rules.rule: Wedding money (份子钱/礼金) goes in a red envelope (wedding-themed ones exist). Amounts depend on closeness and region; LTL gives about 200–1,000 yuan as typical, in even numbers such as 600, 666 or 888. Write your name(s) on the envelope, optionally with a short blessing (some prefer an even number of characters, 好事成双).
rules.why: Weddings are 红事 (red events): even, lucky numbers and red packaging.

rules.rule: Never give red envelopes — cash or electronic — or holiday gifts such as mooncakes to public officials: CC-CEDICT lists “kickback; bribe” among 红包's meanings, and China's discipline inspectors target holiday “隔空送礼” via electronic red envelopes and gifts of mooncakes.
rules.why: What is a family custom can be a bribe outside the family; officials are barred from accepting.

sources.title: Astronomy Engine 2.1.19 (npm astronomy-engine): new moons and solar longitudes, computed by the verifier
sources.publisher: Don Cross (cosinekitty/astronomy); computation script by the verifier (verify-ff/scripts/lunar_check.cjs; library installed with scripts disabled)
sources.evidence: Own computation in Beijing time (UTC+8); month 11 contains the winter solstice; no leap month in either lunar year. New moons: 2026-01-19 03:52 (腊月 starts; 29 days) and 2026-02-17 20:01 → 正月初一 Tue 17 Feb 2026, 除夕 Mon 16 Feb 2026 = 腊月二十九; 2027-01-08 04:25 (腊月 starts: 二十三 = Sat 30 Jan, 二十四 = Sun 31 Jan 2027; 29 days) and 2027-02-06 23:56:47 (three minutes before Beijing midnight) → 正月初一 Sat 6 Feb 2027, 除夕 Fri 5 Feb 2027 = 腊月二十九; next new year 2028-01-26 23:13 → Wed 26 Jan 2028. Festivals: 元宵 Tue 3 Mar 2026 / Sat 20 Feb 2027; 清明 (sun at 15°) 5 Apr 2026 02:40 / 5 Apr 2027 08:17; 端午 Fri 19 Jun 2026 / Wed 9 Jun 2027; 中秋 Fri 25 Sep 2026 / Wed 15 Sep 2027; 重阳 Sun 18 Oct 2026 / Fri 8 Oct 2027. Same results as the researcher's calendar.js decoding and LTL's provisional list.

phrases.literal: 吃 eat + 汤圆 glutinous-rice balls (in soup)
phrases.english: eat tangyuan (sweet rice balls)
phrases.usage: The Lantern Festival food (CCTV 2026: 吃汤圆，庆团圆 — “eat tangyuan, celebrate being together”). 汤圆 is the southern name and the southern, wrapped kind (现代汉语词典: 糯米粉等做的球形食品，大多有馅儿，带汤吃), so a south/central family will most likely say 汤圆.
phrases.speaker: either
phrases.regional_note: South (Jiangsu/Zhejiang-centred): 汤圆, wrapped by hand; some southern families also eat them on the morning of New Year's Day. North (Beijing-centred): 元宵, rolled in rice flour.

phrases.literal: 清明 Qingming + 安康 peace and good health
phrases.english: Peace and good health at Qingming
phrases.usage: Qingming (5 Apr 2026; 5 Apr 2027) is when families honour and tend ancestors' graves. If you send a Qingming message, 清明安康 is the usual safe wish (zhihu: 这种做法较为常见); 安康 = 平安和健康 (现代汉语词典: 祝全家～). The longer 清明节安康 is also used (zhihu greeting images). Do not wish 清明节快乐 to people going to sweep graves. Ordinary greetings such as 早上好 are fine (the “no greetings at Qingming” claim is a rumour, Guangming Online 2025).
phrases.speaker: either

sources.title: 清明节应该怎么祝福？可以“快乐”吗？ - 知乎
sources.publisher: 知乎 Zhihu (community articles)
sources.evidence: Search summary (results also from gmw.cn and thepaper.cn): in zhihu discussions many people still feel Qingming is mainly for honouring ancestors and avoid “快乐”, using “安康” instead — “这种做法较为常见”; safe options listed: 清明安康, 清明节安好, 节日安康.

sources.title: 清明节不能问好是谣言
sources.publisher: 光明网 Guangming Online (reporting the Shanghai rumour-refuting platform)
sources.evidence: Search summary: the Shanghai rumour-refuting platform says ordinary greetings such as “早上好” and “晚上好” break no custom or taboo; very few people wish others “清明节快乐”, but Qingming is not only solemn — “一句‘踏青快乐’就是非常贴切的祝福语”. A related item quotes 高巍 (Beijing Folklore Society) that “不能说清明节快乐” is a claim of the last couple of years.

sources.title: 清明节不能说快乐，只能祝“安康”？答案令人意外……
sources.publisher: 中国新闻网 (China News Service)
sources.evidence: Search-result summary returned by WebSearch on 2026-11-02; the page itself could not be opened from the sandbox (query: 清明节 能说“清明安康”吗 “踏青快乐” 端午节快乐 端午安康 都可以 民俗专家 2026, restricted to Chinese news sites; results also thepaper.cn newsDetail_forward_22586397 “清明节快乐？！可以这样说吗”, chinanews 2017-04-01 “清明节可以互祝快乐么？有专家称“可以说””, sd.chinanews.com.cn 2022-04-04, gmw.cn 2022-04-03, gmw.cn 2025-04-03 “官方辟谣清明节不能问好”, politics.people.com.cn 2014-04-05 “民俗专家萧放：清明又称踏青节”; no 2026 article; the summary did not always say which page a line came from). Lines: 高巍 (Beijing Folklore Society): “清明节快乐” can be said and the “cannot” claim is only a couple of years old; Shandong folklorist 朱振华: Qingming is for both tomb sweeping and outings, so 快乐 is fine; a 2025 rumour-refuting report: “踏青快乐” is an apt wish, though few people say “清明节快乐” because of the tomb visits; chinanews 2025: the claim “端午不能‘快乐’只能‘安康’” appeared suddenly in 2015; a 2017 scholar: 端午安康 fits better from the anti-disease angle.

sources.title: 清明节不能问好是谣言

sources.evidence: Search summary: the Shanghai rumour-refuting platform says ordinary greetings such as “早上好” and “晚上好” break no custom or taboo; very few people wish others “清明节快乐”, but Qingming is not only solemn — “一句‘踏青快乐’就是非常贴切的祝福语”. sources.title: 清明节不能说快乐，只能祝“安康”？答案令人意外……
sources.publisher: 中国新闻网 (China News Service)
sources.evidence: Search-result summary returned by WebSearch on 2026-11-02; the page itself could not be opened from the sandbox (query: 清明节 能说“清明安康”吗 “踏青快乐” 端午节快乐 端午安康 都可以 民俗专家 2026, restricted to Chinese news sites; results also thepaper.cn newsDetail_forward_22586397 “清明节快乐？！可以这样说吗”, chinanews 2017-04-01 “清明节可以互祝快乐么？有专家称“可以说””, sd.chinanews.com.cn 2022-04-04, gmw.cn 2022-04-03, gmw.cn 2025-04-03 “官方辟谣清明节不能问好”, politics.people.com.cn 2014-04-05 “民俗专家萧放：清明又称踏青节”; no 2026 article; the summary did not always say which page a line came from). Lines: 高巍 (Beijing Folklore Society): “清明节快乐” can be said and the “cannot” claim is only a couple of years old; Shandong folklorist 朱振华: Qingming is for both tomb sweeping and outings, so 快乐 is fine; a 2025 rumour-refuting report: “踏青快乐” is an apt wish, though few people say “清明节快乐” because of the tomb visits; chinanews 2025: the claim “端午不能‘快乐’只能‘安康’” appeared suddenly in 2015; a 2017 scholar: 端午安康 fits better from the anti-disease angle.

phrases.pinyin_as_source: 奶奶 nǎinai (CC-CEDICT nai3 nai5; 现代汉语词典 nǎi•nai)
phrases.literal: 奶奶 Grandma + 祝 wish + 您 you (polite) + 生日快乐 happy birthday
phrases.english: Happy birthday, Grandma!
phrases.usage: Polite birthday wish for the partner's grandparents, parents and other older relatives: family title first, then 祝您生日快乐 (slot). It is a slot change of the official HSK 3 sample line 姐，祝您生日快乐！ (a younger brother to his elder sister); HSK 4 has 祝爸爸生日快乐. For elderly relatives add a long-life wish (祝您生日快乐，健康长寿！). With people of your own generation 你 is the usual choice: 祝你生日快乐！ (HSK 3).
phrases.speaker: me
phrases.regional_note: 您 is used far more in the north (especially Beijing) — the HSK sample even uses it to an elder sister — while many southern families say 你 to relatives in everyday talk; 您 to an elder is always polite (forum discussions; anecdotal).

checked_sources.title: 您 (discussion thread)
checked_sources.publisher: Chinese-forums.com
checked_sources.evidence: Search-result summary returned by WebSearch on 2026-11-02; the page itself could not be opened from the sandbox (query: 南方人很少说“您” 北方人常用“您” 南北差异 称呼长辈; results also chinese-forums.com “Is 你 or 您 more appropriate here”, silkmandarin.cn blog 2020). Anecdotal: forum users say many southern dialects have no honorific equivalent of 您, so many southerners do not habitually use it, while it is common in the north (Beijing); with elders, teachers and people of higher status 您 is still expected.

phrases.literal: 祝 wish + 您 you (polite) + 健康 healthy + 长寿 long-lived
phrases.english: Wishing you good health and a long life!
phrases.usage: The wish for elderly people — at New Year (CCTV) and as the long-life wish at their birthdays (birthday wishes for elders centre on long life: 长命百岁, 福寿安康 — zhihu). Adapted (slot) from wishes to elderly people reported by CCTV: 祝你们生活幸福、健康长寿 (Premier Li Qiang in a care home) and 祝他们健康长寿、春节快乐 (Xi Jinping); for one grandparent use 您. Combine with the birthday wish (祝您生日快乐 + 健康长寿).
phrases.speaker: me

slots.meaning: who you wish it to: 您 one elder, 你们 several people

phrases.literal: 福 blessings + 如 like + 东海 the East Sea; 寿 life-span + 比 compare + 南山 the Southern Mountains
phrases.english: May your happiness be as boundless as the East Sea and your life as long as the Southern Mountains!
phrases.usage: The classic toast for an elderly person's big birthday (traditionally from 60: 60, 70, 80…); 现代汉语词典: 用作对老年人的祝颂（多与“福如东海”连用）. The Xinhua idiom data calls 福如东海 a 旧时祝颂语 (traditional blessing), but it lives on as THE set toast at elders' birthdays — zhihu calls the longer couplet 福如东海长流水，寿比南山不老松 the most common birthday blessing for elders. Formal and fixed: say it as a toast or write it in a card, not as everyday conversation.
phrases.speaker: me

sources.evidence: Search summary of this and related posts (zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/691462189, /p/638411414; chinanews.com.cn 2011-07-29 “孝德习俗：儿女如何给长辈‘做大寿’”): “福如东海长流水，寿比南山不老松” is the most common birthday blessing for elders; other common wishes: 长命百岁, 身体健康, 笑口常开, 福寿安康; traditionally birthdays below 50 are not called 寿 and 做寿 starts at 60; 庆九不庆十 (celebrate the 9, not the round 10) in some places, as a full number is felt unlucky; long-life noodles (寿面) and longevity peaches (寿桃) are eaten after the birthday greetings; customs differ a lot by region.

sources.evidence: Search summary of folk-custom articles (also zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/58163408, /p/397056070, /p/365849283): when handing over the money, saying “请节哀顺变” is common; amounts: “民间普遍认为要用单数” in many areas (e.g. 100, 300, 500 counted in hundreds), but some areas have no such taboo; avoid amounts with 6, 8, 9 such as 366, 288, 399; “这个礼金千万不能用红纸包装，最好用白色或素色纸封套包好，在封皮上写上‘奠仪’、‘帛金’之类的黑字并署名”; older banknotes are better (brand-new ones suggest you prepared in advance); give the money at the condolence visit, not after the burial; dress soberly. Practice varies by region.

rules.rule: The Lantern Festival (正月十五) closes the New Year season: lanterns, lantern riddles, and sweet glutinous-rice balls. In the north they are 元宵 (filling rolled in rice flour), in the south 汤圆 (wrapped like dumplings) — “‘元宵’是北方人的叫法，‘汤圆’是南方人的称呼”.
rules.why: Using the family's own word (likely 汤圆 for a south/central family) sounds natural.
rules.regional_note: South centred on Jiangsu/Zhejiang: 汤圆 (some eat them on New Year's morning too); north centred on Beijing: 元宵.

rules.rule: Qingming is for honouring ancestors (tomb sweeping) and also for spring outings. Do not wish people “清明节快乐” in connection with grave visits; 清明安康 is the common safe wish, 踏青快乐 fits an outing, and ordinary greetings (早上好 etc.) are fine — the claim that you may not greet anyone at Qingming is a rumour.
rules.why: A cheerful “快乐” clashes with mourning; folklorists note that the outright ban on 快乐 is itself recent, but most people avoid it.

sources.title: 清明节不能问好是谣言
sources.publisher: 光明网 Guangming Online (reporting the Shanghai rumour-refuting platform)
sources.evidence: Search summary: the Shanghai rumour-refuting platform says ordinary greetings such as “早上好” and “晚上好” break no custom or taboo; very few people wish others “清明节快乐”, but Qingming is not only solemn — “一句‘踏青快乐’就是非常贴切的祝福语”. A related item quotes 高巍 (Beijing Folklore Society) that “不能说清明节快乐” is a claim of the last couple of years.

sources.title: 清明节应该怎么祝福？可以“快乐”吗？ - 知乎
sources.publisher: 知乎 Zhihu (community articles)
sources.evidence: Search summary (results also from gmw.cn and thepaper.cn): in zhihu discussions many people still feel Qingming is mainly for honouring ancestors and avoid “快乐”, using “安康” instead — “这种做法较为常见”; safe options listed: 清明安康, 清明节安好, 节日安康.

sources.title: 清明节快乐？！可以这样说吗……
sources.publisher: 澎湃新闻 The Paper
sources.evidence: Search summary: 高巍, secretary-general of the Beijing Folklore Society, says “不能说清明节快乐” only appeared in the last couple of years; Qingming also includes spring outings (踏青), so “快乐” is not wrong in itself.

sources.title: 清明节不能说快乐，只能祝“安康”？答案令人意外……
sources.publisher: 中国新闻网 (China News Service)
sources.evidence: Search-result summary returned by WebSearch on 2026-11-02; the page itself could not be opened from the sandbox (query: 清明节 能说“清明安康”吗 “踏青快乐” 端午节快乐 端午安康 都可以 民俗专家 2026, restricted to Chinese news sites; results also thepaper.cn newsDetail_forward_22586397 “清明节快乐？！可以这样说吗”, chinanews 2017-04-01 “清明节可以互祝快乐么？有专家称“可以说””, sd.chinanews.com.cn 2022-04-04, gmw.cn 2022-04-03, gmw.cn 2025-04-03 “官方辟谣清明节不能问好”, politics.people.com.cn 2014-04-05 “民俗专家萧放：清明又称踏青节”; no 2026 article; the summary did not always say which page a line came from). Lines: 高巍 (Beijing Folklore Society): “清明节快乐” can be said and the “cannot” claim is only a couple of years old; Shandong folklorist 朱振华: Qingming is for both tomb sweeping and outings, so 快乐 is fine; a 2025 rumour-refuting report: “踏青快乐” is an apt wish, though few people say “清明节快乐” because of the tomb visits; chinanews 2025: the claim “端午不能‘快乐’只能‘安康’” appeared suddenly in 2015; a 2017 scholar: 端午安康 fits better from the anti-disease angle.

rules.rule: Dragon Boat Festival: both 端午安康 and 端午节快乐 are correct (Guangming Online, 2026). 端午安康 is now very common — CCTV uses it — while the claim that 快乐 is forbidden started as a 2015 internet rumour; historians of custom stress that Duanwu was always a festive day.
rules.why: The rumour still circulates (debunking articles reappear every year), so 端午安康 avoids any discussion; 快乐 is not a mistake.

rules.rule: Mid-Autumn is a family-reunion festival (中秋节又称“团圆节”, HSK 6 sample): families gather, eat mooncakes and admire the moon. Mooncakes are given to relatives, friends, colleagues and business partners — plain boxes for acquaintances, elaborate ones for important clients; boxes commonly hold four or eight; the receiver does not open the box in front of the giver and reciprocates later. Officials may not accept such gifts (2025 discipline notice on 违规收送月饼).
rules.why: Mid-Autumn is about reunion (CCTV: 吃月饼，话团圆), and round mooncakes (现代汉语词典: 圆形有馅儿的点心) are the standard seasonal gift.

Zhōngqiū Kuàilè! Happy Mid-Autumn Festival!” as the short form for messages and cards; 祝您全家幸福 (zhù nín quán jiā xìng fú) “a polite option”; mooncakes are exchanged with relatives, friends, colleagues and business partners; plain boxes for acquaintances, elaborate boxes for an important client; boxes commonly hold four or eight; “You don’t typically open the box in front of the giver”, and it is polite to reciprocate if a colleague gifts you mooncakes. The summary did not say which page each line came from.

rules.rule: Birthdays of elders are 寿: traditionally only birthdays from about 60 are celebrated as 做寿/祝寿, with the round decades (大寿: 60, 70, 80) the big ones; some places celebrate the year before the round number (庆九不庆十). Long-life noodles (寿面) and peach-shaped buns (寿桃) are served, and guests offer long-life wishes (福如东海，寿比南山; 健康长寿; 长命百岁). Customs differ by region — ask which birthday the family is celebrating.
rules.why: Longevity is the central wish for the old; age counting and the “9 not 10” custom vary between regions.
rules.regional_note: “庆九不庆十” and the age at which 做寿 starts vary by region and family (zhihu).

sources.title: 过寿不能随便过，“庆九不庆十”，73、84也不过，寿礼禁忌讲究多 - 知乎
sources.publisher: 知乎 Zhihu (community articles)
sources.evidence: Search summary of this and related posts (zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/691462189, /p/638411414; chinanews.com.cn 2011-07-29 “孝德习俗：儿女如何给长辈‘做大寿’”): “福如东海长流水，寿比南山不老松” is the most common birthday blessing for elders; other common wishes: 长命百岁, 身体健康, 笑口常开, 福寿安康; traditionally birthdays below 50 are not called 寿 and 做寿 starts at 60; 庆九不庆十 (celebrate the 9, not the round 10) in some places, as a full number is felt unlucky; long-life noodles (寿面) and longevity peaches (寿桃) are eaten after the birthday greetings; customs differ a lot by region.

rules.rule: At weddings say 新婚快乐 and add a four-character blessing such as 百年好合 or 白头偕老 (a 新婚颂词 pair in 现代汉语词典); relatives often add 早生贵子. Wedding money goes in a red envelope in an even, lucky amount (see the red-envelope scene).
rules.why: Weddings are red, even-numbered “happy events” (红事).

rules.rule: Condolences: keep it short — 请节哀(顺变). Condolence money (礼金, written 奠仪 or 帛金 on the envelope) goes in a white or plain envelope, never a red one; many regions use odd amounts (one article also advises avoiding 6, 8 and 9), and older notes are preferred; give it at the condolence visit, not afterwards; dress soberly.
rules.why: Funerals are 白事: the colours and numbers are the reverse of red, happy events.
rules.regional_note: Odd versus even amounts and other details vary by region (some areas have no odd-number custom); ask the family.

sources.title: 葬礼送悼念花圈也得随礼吗？丧事礼金给多少？封包写法有何讲究？ - 知乎
sources.publisher: 知乎 Zhihu (community articles)
sources.evidence: Search summary of folk-custom articles (also zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/58163408, /p/397056070, /p/365849283): when handing over the money, saying “请节哀顺变” is common; amounts: “民间普遍认为要用单数” in many areas (e.g. 100, 300, 500 counted in hundreds), but some areas have no such taboo; avoid amounts with 6, 8, 9 such as 366, 288, 399; “这个礼金千万不能用红纸包装，最好用白色或素色纸封套包好，在封皮上写上‘奠仪’、‘帛金’之类的黑字并署名”; older banknotes are better (brand-new ones suggest you prepared in advance); give the money at the condolence visit, not after the burial; dress soberly. Practice varies by region.
